items.impact: Builders receive a concrete directory-level package contract with an index, manifest, ordered exact-source shards, and audit evidence.
items.statement: The policy establishes Document Sets as deterministic directory artifacts for long Markdown and text outputs while keeping plan shards and plan-graph shards outside this artifact family.
items.title: Document Set package boundary is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: - `generated_at`
4. **Clean-room determinism:** regeneration in an empty temp directory yields byte-identical `00-index.md`, `manifest.json`, shard files, and audit evidence hashes.

items.impact: A wall-clock timestamp makes audit JSON and its hash differ across clean-room regenerations, while an input-derived timestamp needs an explicit derivation rule. Implementations can satisfy either the field or byte identity but cannot prove both consistently from this text.
items.statement: The required `generated_at` field has no deterministic value rule even though audit evidence must be byte-identical in clean-room regeneration.
items.title: Audit timestamps conflict with byte-identical evidence

evidence.exact_quote: - `<slug>` is lowercase kebab-case from split heading text; fallback slug is `chunk-<start_line>-<end_line>`

items.impact: Unicode-equivalent headings, punctuation-only headings, duplicate headings, reserved filenames, and length limits can produce collisions or platform-dependent paths. The fallback only addresses absent heading text, not collisions or unsafe normalized results.
items.statement: Heading-derived shard names lack a complete canonicalization, collision, reserved-name, and maximum-length contract for untrusted source headings.
items.title: Heading-derived filenames are under-specified

evidence.exact_quote: Every packaging run MUST execute all three audits:

items.impact: A package cannot pass through sampling or a partial audit suite; reconstruction, manifest/index agreement, and clean-room output equality all have named evidence surfaces.
items.statement: The policy requires three full-coverage audits on every packaging run and makes missing or failed audit evidence run-fatal for over-budget tracked artifacts.
items.title: Full-coverage package verification is non-bypassable

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Document Packaging Policy defines deterministic packaging for long Markdown/text artifacts under .puppet-master/** into Document Sets, while Plans/_shards/** remains process-mirror output and plan graph remains the separate sharded JSON mechanism under .puppet-master/project/plan_graph/index.json with nodes/<node_id>.json shards.

canonical_text: A Document Set is a directory artifact containing 00-index.md, manifest.json, ordered NN-*.md or NN-*.txt shard files with exact source segments, and an evidence/ directory for audits A/B/C.

items.impact: The atomized units keep package ownership separate from repository-generated plan shards and project plan-graph storage.
items.statement: DPP-002 and DPP-003 preserve both the package boundary and the required Document Set members without claiming ownership of plan-shard outputs.
items.title: Scope and directory contract remain atomized

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: 00-index.md must expose source logical path, deterministic generation marker from source_sha256, source sha256, split rule summary, ordered shard listing with filenames and line ranges, and the fixed generated-file warning.

canonical_text: manifest.json must include source_path, source_sha256, source_line_count, split_rule, audit_files, and canonical shards[] entries with order, filename, start_line, end_line, segment_sha256, and byte_count.

items.impact: Different builders can choose incompatible JSON versions, numeric/string representations, object ordering, marker encodings, and path encodings while each includes every named field. Byte-identical clean-room output is therefore not fully falsifiable across independent implementations.
items.statement: The index and manifest enumerate required fields but do not define a schema version, canonical JSON serialization, path encoding, or the generation-marker derivation algorithm.
items.title: Manifest bytes are not independently reproducible

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: 'Shard filenames are deterministic: numbering starts at 01, zero padding width is max(2, digits(total_shards)), filename format is <zero_padded_index>-<slug>.<ext>, and generated .docset/** members must not become packaging inputs.'

canonical_text: Document packages may preserve local auth, provider/account, connect-health, runtime lifecycle, durability, attribution, and provider-facade evidence, but interpretation remains routed to the owning docs and file hints alone never prove readiness.

items.impact: A package can contain sensitive account or runtime evidence and create heading-derived paths, but the unit set does not state permission, redaction, retention, symlink, traversal, or atomic-open rules. Owner routing avoids semantic overreach but does not protect package bytes.
items.statement: DPP-006 and DPP-007 define recursion exclusion and interpretation ownership, but leave untrusted path handling and sensitive evidence lifecycle to builder discretion.
items.title: Package files lack security and privacy lifecycle rules

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Command and event seam evidence packages keep contradictions visible, including chat.thread.created versus chat.thread_created, terminal run names, requested/effective/runtime mode splits, reserved-name ownership, and /compact owner evidence.

canonical_text: 'Worktree evidence packages preserve surface ownership: Source Control is the primary operational surface, Orchestrator consumes worktree identity and recovery views, and Settings surfaces expose configuration and diagnostics rather than primary active-worktree management.'

items.impact: Packaging preserves conflicts as evidence and routes operational UI authority to the named surfaces rather than silently selecting a command name or taking over worktree management.
items.statement: DPP-008 and DPP-009 intentionally preserve command contradictions and worktree surface ownership without promoting packaging prose into an owner contract.
items.title: Contradiction evidence retains owner boundaries

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Consumer-drift packages flag mechanical stale examples and preserve glossary artifacts, requirements-staging seglog artifacts, package-generation lineage states, and the distinction between packaging evidence and execution evidence when both use evidence/ naming.

canonical_text: UI command evidence packages preserve consumer splits for UI_Command_Catalog, blocked/HITL mutator ownership, account and concern promotion flows, and wizard_step meaning without making the base target wizard-shaped.

items.impact: Consumers can distinguish packaging evidence from execution proof and avoid treating wizard-specific command context as a universal target shape.
items.statement: DPP-010 and DPP-011 retain consumer-drift markers, artifact lineage, evidence-kind distinctions, and UI command ownership splits.
items.title: Consumer evidence does not erase command context

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Migration and reversible-action evidence keeps Widget_System and FinalGUISpec on one mirrored migration rule, and limits immediate_undo to direct undo or /revert within practical reversible local presentation/layout and editor-level windows.

canonical_text: Provider/account and event/command routing packages expose account, non-provider identity, command routing, local SSOT disagreement, subject-open requirements, and stale FileManager consumer boundaries.

items.impact: Independent builders can choose different undo expiry semantics and different identity resolvers, creating incompatible user behavior and stale-consumer recovery paths with no pass/fail oracle.
items.statement: The phrase `practical` does not define the immediate-undo transition window, and exposing subject-open and stale consumer boundaries does not define which owner resolves identity or how failure recovers.
items.title: Undo and identity seams lack executable resolution rules

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: 'Attention and blocked-state evidence remains scoped: a project can be background_active with attention_required without being globally blocked, and blocked_episode does not expand the policy into a blocked-episode-shaped payload family.'

canonical_text: Owner/consumer reconciliation packages preserve modern canonical field names separately from stale canonical scope language, so transfer cleanup does not mistake newer labels for complete owner alignment.

items.impact: Consumers are prevented from presenting all attention as a global block and from treating updated field names as proof that old scope boundaries were repaired.
items.statement: DPP-014 and DPP-015 explicitly preserve modern-name versus stale-scope distinctions and `attention_required` versus globally `blocked` state semantics.
items.title: Attention is not collapsed into blocked state

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Generated-doc and preview evidence packages must not leak path assumptions back into routing, and must preserve the FileManager path-open versus assistant-chat open-by-identity consumer split.
- /open-by-identity

items.impact: The policy can preserve evidence of the split but cannot tell FileManager, assistant chat, generated-doc previews, or artifact openers which identity fields, errors, or fallback transitions to implement.
items.statement: DPP-016 labels command and re-audit splits, while DPP-017 names an open-by-identity seam without defining the primitive, caller set, response contract, or path-open migration behavior.
items.title: Open-by-identity remains a named but unowned seam

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: 'Primary split must occur at Markdown headings beginning with ## outside fenced code blocks, while heading-like lines inside fences opened by triple backticks or ~~~ are ignored until matching fence delimiters close the active context.'
canonical_text: If primary split does not produce valid bounded shards, the splitter must use deterministic fixed line chunks and record fallback parameters in manifest.json.split_rule uniformly.

items.impact: Variable-length Markdown fences, indentation, info strings, a mismatched closing length, or EOF inside an open fence can lead implementations to split at different lines. `Valid bounded shards` also has no numeric validity predicate beyond the separate fallback default.
items.statement: DPP-018 and DPP-019 define the primary and fallback split paths but not a complete fence parser, unterminated-fence failure state, or exact bounded-shard predicate.
items.title: Split fallback depends on undefined validity semantics

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Packaging triggers when max_bytes, max_estimated_tokens, or fallback_chunk_lines thresholds are reached; these deterministic defaults are recorded in Plans/auto_decisions.jsonl and reused unless superseded by a higher-precedence SSOT source.

canonical_text: A packaged Document Set must prove reconstruction hash equality, complete line accounting, idempotency, and clean-room determinism; packaging is only a file-boundary transformation and must not rewrite source bytes, normalize line endings, or clean up content.

items.impact: Character counting, byte encoding, threshold boundary evaluation, and which higher-precedence decision snapshot governs regeneration can drift while losslessness still passes. A package may therefore be generated or skipped differently across implementations.
items.statement: DPP-020 names trigger defaults and DPP-021 gives strong byte-preservation proofs, but the trigger measurement encoding and the identity of the effective override decision are not captured in the package contract.
items.title: Lossless output can still have inconsistent trigger decisions

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Every packaging run must execute Audit A, Audit B, and Audit C at full coverage with no sampling, write deterministic audit JSON files under evidence/, and include audit_id, source_path, source_sha256, status, generated_at, and details.

canonical_text: Document Packaging enforcement covers requirements builder staging outputs, canonical project Markdown/text artifacts, and any subsystem writing Markdown/text under .puppet-master/** through the same writer abstraction; a tracked over-budget artifact without a valid passing Document Set must fail the run.

items.impact: Tracked writers have an unambiguous fail-closed result when a required package or any full-coverage audit is absent or invalid.
items.statement: DPP-022 and DPP-023 bind full audit coverage to non-bypassable run failure for over-budget artifacts written through the governed abstraction.
items.title: Governed writers fail closed on invalid packages

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: When packaging triggers for a Markdown/text logical artifact path, the canonical packaged form is a .docset directory named by appending .docset to the complete filename including extension.
gui_classification_reason: This unit concerns user-visible file/path presentation.
canonical_text: 'The Document Set directory reuses the contract contents: 00-index.md, manifest.json, NN-*.md or NN-*.txt shards, and evidence/ directory.'

items.impact: A builder can mark the unit GUI-complete based only on a filesystem naming rule even though no visible label, canonical-state indicator, error state, accessible announcement, localization rule, or user action is specified.
items.statement: DPP-024 is classified GUI-related because a path may be user-visible, but DPP-024 and DPP-025 only define filesystem names and members, not a GUI presentation or interaction contract.
items.title: GUI-related metadata overstates visible behavior

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: When packaging produces a .docset/ directory, the original file path remains as a deterministic pointer stub with canonical-content statement, entrypoint <filename>.docset/00-index.md, source_sha256, and puppet-master docset verify <docset_path> command.

items.impact: Existing consumers retain a file at the logical path and can discover both the canonical entrypoint and the deterministic verification command.
items.statement: DPP-026 fixes pointer-stub presence and the fields needed to locate and verify the canonical Document Set.
items.title: Pointer stubs preserve logical-path discovery

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: When a .docset/ directory exists for an artifact, that directory is canonical and the pointer stub file is derived; without a .docset/ directory, the logical .md or .txt file is canonical.

items.impact: Concurrent readers can observe a new directory with an old stub, a new stub before a complete directory, or deletion during regeneration. Existence alone can incorrectly promote a partial directory to canonical truth.
items.statement: DPP-027 defines the two steady canonical states but not the atomic transition, readiness marker, locking model, or crash recovery between source-file and docset canonicality.
items.title: Canonical truth flips on directory existence without a transaction

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Pointer-stub verification requires the .docset/ directory, .docset/manifest.json, and all reconstruction sha256, line coverage, index/manifest, idempotency, and clean-room checks; verification fails for missing docset, failed checks, or over-budget source without docset.

- Repairs `sfk-2ebbc3349354d2a57460398b`: packaging validation failure uses exit code `42`, error shape `{error_code, message, failed_rule_id, document_path, partial_outputs[]}`, and rollback rule "delete temp outputs; never overwrite previous packaged output until all checks pass."

items.impact: Exit code and temp-output deletion are now explicit, but concurrent generation versus verification, process death during cleanup, ownership of orphan cleanup, and whether `partial_outputs[]` includes pre-existing outputs remain undefined.
items.statement: DPP-028 defines verification failure conditions, and the addendum supplies an error and rollback shape, but the concurrency and orphaned-temp recovery state machine remains open.
items.title: Failure rollback is explicit but not concurrency-safe

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The requirements.md example preserves the canonical pointer-stub and requirements.md.docset/ directory shape, ordered shard examples, audit filenames, example source hash, and deterministic verify command.

items.impact: The preserved example communicates shape but cannot be run as a golden fixture because its source hash and shard set are placeholders. It therefore cannot independently catch filename, hash, or pointer formatting drift.
items.statement: DPP-029 treats a truncated hash and ellipsis-bearing tree as the canonical example, leaving example-based acceptance non-falsifiable.
items.title: Requirements example is illustrative rather than testable

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The former Document Packaging Policy source-preserving bridge is retired in place after Phase 2B atomized or structurally dispositioned Document_Packaging_Policy-S0001 through Document_Packaging_Policy-S0028 into DPP-002 through DPP-029, explicit structural coverage, and retired bridge lineage. DPP-001 remains only as migration lineage for the retired bridge span and must not re-own atomized source coverage.

Phase 2B batch 047 atomized `Document_Packaging_Policy-S0001` through `Document_Packaging_Policy-S0023` into `DPP-002` through `DPP-029`, with structural parent spans `Document_Packaging_Policy-S0007` and `Document_Packaging_Policy-S0017` mapped to their child units while preserving anchor alias `7`. Phase 2B batch 048 structurally dispositioned `Document_Packaging_Policy-S0024`, `S0025`, `S0026`, and `S0028`, and retired `DPP-001` as migration-lineage compatibility coverage for `Document_Packaging_Policy-S0027`. `Plans/Document_Packaging_Policy.md` now has no residual source-preserving product coverage. These batches did not update Spec Lock, generated shards, evidence bundles, auto_decisions, or plan_graph, and did not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, or executable build tasks.

- Repairs `sfk-803c53af977a001393cd07fc`: SSOT naming contradictions are not permanent policy. Each contradiction row must name `resolution_owner_doc`, `resolution_due_phase`, and `current_status`. Until resolved, consumers must use owner-doc names from `Plans/00-plans-index.md` over examples in packaging prose.

items.impact: The accepted PlanUnit map says all product coverage was atomized before the later addendum introduced mandatory contradiction lifecycle fields, owner-name precedence, an exit code, an error schema, and rollback behavior. PlanUnit-driven builders can omit those canonical rules while appearing fully covered.
items.statement: DPP-001 is retired as migration-only lineage and the migration prose claims no residual source-preserving product coverage, but the later FABLE addendum adds product contracts that are not represented by DPP-002 through DPP-029.
items.title: Post-atomization addendum is outside the PlanUnit coverage claim

segments.summary: The source-level policy is unusually concrete on package shape, losslessness, and full audits, but deterministic timestamps, hostile filename inputs, canonical serialization, sensitive evidence lifecycle, and transaction semantics remain unresolved.

DPP-002 through DPP-009 preserve scope, members, evidence routing, contradiction visibility, and surface ownership; canonical serialization and filesystem/privacy controls are the main negative-space failures.

DPP-010 through DPP-017 accurately preserve consumer drift and state distinctions, while undo expiry, identity resolution, open-by-identity caller coverage, and failure behavior remain non-executable.

DPP-018 through DPP-025 provide the split, trigger, proof, audit, enforcement, and directory rules; fence validity, measurement snapshots, and a GUI classification without GUI behavior remain material ambiguities.

DPP-026 through DPP-029 cover pointer discovery, steady canonical states, verification, and an example, but atomic state transitions and executable fixtures are absent; the later FABLE product addendum also falls outside the declared atomized PlanUnit coverage.
